description:
**amphora has no `ROADMAP.md`, no `CLAUDE.md`, no `CHANGELOG.md` and — for a library intended for reuse — no `LICENSE`.** It scores 1 of 5 on the portfolio's own documentation standard, the lowest of any repo audited on 2026-08-25.

The missing LICENSE is the sharpest of these. This is a library whose whole point is to be adopted by other applications, and a repository with no licence grants nothing: a would-be consumer has no permission to use it, and that is true regardless of intent. It also blocks the eventual publish/distribute question entirely.

**The missing ROADMAP matters for a specific reason here.** The repo's central claims are currently unfalsifiable rather than false — the code is real (4,868 lines across both ports, one TODO), the environment docs are exemplary, and yet nothing has moved a byte. A reader has no single place that says so plainly. `docs/reference/environment-matrix.md` and `environment-evidence.md` are the model to follow: every environmental cell honestly reads `NOT YET VERIFIED — physical device`, and they explicitly refuse to substitute simulator results for hardware ones. That discipline should set the tone for the roadmap rather than being buried two directories down.

**`README.md` is also five tasklists stale** (last touched `c04fefd`): it still asserts *"Nothing moves bytes yet"* — currently true — alongside *"No conformance vectors yet"*, which is false, and lists as *Stubbed* work that `60`/`70` closed.

Deliberately LAST in this batch. A roadmap written before `100`–`120` run would describe intentions; written after, it describes a measured position.

userStories.title: The repository grants permission to use it
acceptanceCriteria: A `LICENSE` file exists, chosen deliberately rather than by default, with the choice's reasoning recorded. This is a client library meant to be embedded in other applications, so the licence directly determines who may adopt it.

The choice accounts for what the repo depends on and what it deliberately does not vendor — the wire protocol is `draft-ietf-httpbis-resumable-upload` against tusd, and the web path uses `tus-js-client` unmodified, so nothing here re-specifies a protocol or carries a copyleft obligation inward. Verify that rather than assuming it.
SPDX headers or a stated file-level convention, consistent with how sibling repos in this portfolio express licence posture.
userStories.notes: LICENSE (MIT) added at root; reasoning + dependency audit recorded in docs/reference/licensing.md. Choice verified, not assumed: iOS has zero external deps (ios/Package.swift); Android runtime deps all Apache-2.0 read from POM <licenses> on Google Maven / Maven Central; junit 4.13.2 EPL-1.0 and org.json 20240303 Public Domain are testImplementation only (org.json POM confirmed the 'Good, not Evil' clause is absent); tus-js-client and TUSKit are NOT dependencies of this repo at all (prose only); tusd v2.4.0 MIT, and MinIO — the one AGPL-3.0 component — is an unmodified upstream container in the integration harness, never linked or distributed, so nothing travels inward. package-lock.json license fields across all 498 transitive dev packages: 426 MIT, 38 ISC, 12 BSD-3, 11 Apache-2.0, 6 BSD-2, 2 0BSD, 1 CC-BY-4.0, 1 (MIT OR CC0-1.0), 1 (BSD-3-Clause OR GPL-2.0) dual — zero unilateral copyleft. File-level convention stated: root LICENSE authoritative, SPDX-License-Identifier in each distributable manifest (package.json already declared MIT; added SPDX comments to ios/Package.swift and android/build.gradle.kts), no per-file headers. Verify: Swift build PASS, Swift tests PASS (46 passed), TypeScript typecheck PASS, 0 failed; Gradle build SKIPPED (no JDK on this machine) so the android/build.gradle.kts edit is unverified locally and runs in CI.

userStories.title: A roadmap that states the measured position, not the intended one
acceptanceCriteria: `ROADMAP.md` opens with where this actually is, in the register `docs/reference/environment-matrix.md` already uses — honest cells, no substitution of a simulator result for a hardware one.

Phases are named for what remains: making the gate total, making the vectors binding, repairing the real-wire environment, closing the ~40 `NOT YET VERIFIED` device cells, the storage governor under genuine pressure (the original `TransferUtility` bug reproduced then shown retired), host adoption via the RN TurboModule, and publication.

Non-goals are stated: no web transfer code, no re-specification of the protocol, no chunk temp files. The third is a design commitment worth protecting in writing, since it is the one a future contributor is most likely to 'optimise' away.
Open decisions are listed, including the placeholder name and whether device evidence can ever be automated.
The roadmap reflects what `100`–`120` MEASURED. If any of those reported UNVERIFIABLE HERE, the roadmap says so rather than rounding it up.
userStories.notes: ROADMAP.md written after 100-120 ran, so it records a measured position. Opens with a 14-row evidence table in the environment-matrix register (AUTOMATED / MANUAL-ON-DEVICE / NOT YET VERIFIED, each cell naming its source); no simulator result is substituted for a hardware one and all 40 device cells (10 rows x 4 columns) stay NOT YET VERIFIED. Seven phases named for what remains: total gate, binding vectors, gated real-wire environment, the 40 device cells, storage governor under genuine pressure (TransferUtility bug reproduced FIRST, then shown retired), RN TurboModule host adoption, publication. Three non-goals stated, with no-chunk-temp-files argued at length as a protected commitment backed by the 3 I6 vectors and the drift control. Open decisions listed: placeholder name (embedded in @amphora/react-native, dev.amphora, module Amphora, AmphoraSpec), whether device evidence can EVER be automated (marked load-bearing - phase 4 has no schedule until answered), the two unwritten ADRs, BackgroundSessionManager's unowned concurrency model, and the visibility/billing dependency. MEASURED, NOT ROUNDED UP: latest CI run 33044503283 (head f769a6f) is RED - ios FAILURE (NetworkGovernor.swift:23 captured var self, TUSKitTransport.swift:27 non-Sendable session), android FAILURE (:android:kaptReleaseKotlin 'Empty schema file'); react-native, conformance-fixture, verify-policy SUCCESS. The android failure is NONDETERMINISTIC and the roadmap says so: job was SUCCESS at 89583f9 and FAILURE at f769a6f with `git diff 89583f9 f769a6f` = one JSON tasklist file, no Kotlin. Also reported unverified rather than rounded up: the Swift real-wire run is local-only (the ios job dies at compile, so swift run + Swift drift control never execute in CI), and Gradle SKIPS on this machine so every Android claim rests on CI alone. New finding not previously recorded anywhere: the RN package's codegen spec AmphoraSpec has NO native implementation - grep for it and for RCTBridgeModule / ReactContextBaseJavaModule across Swift/Kotlin/ObjC/headers returns nothing, and there is no podspec or Gradle module for the package. Indexed in docs/README.md ('unlinked is unreachable') and linked from README.md; docs/reference/licensing.md's forward-link ../../ROADMAP.md now resolves. Link check across all four files: 0 broken. Verify: .chief/verify.sh 3 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed - PASS Swift build, PASS Swift tests (46 passed), PASS TypeScript typecheck, SKIPPED Gradle (no JDK on PATH); docs-only change, nothing Android-touching, so the skip leaves nothing in this story unverified.

userStories.title: README stops contradicting the tree
acceptanceCriteria: The claims that no conformance vectors exist and that work is Stubbed are corrected — `Tests/Conformance/vectors.json` holds 40 vectors and `60`/`70` closed the stubs.
'Nothing moves bytes yet' is updated to whatever `120` established, in either direction. If bytes still have not moved, it stays and says why.

A `CLAUDE.md` is added covering what a session working here needs: the no-chunk-temp-files commitment, the local-skip vs CI-fail gate distinction, that `ios/Package.swift` declares tests as an `.executableTarget` so `swift test` reports 'no tests found' while `swift run AmphoraPathTests` passes, and the adopt-the-protocol/build-the-clients boundary.

A `CHANGELOG.md` is started. It is missing in every repo audited, so this is the portfolio's most-ignored standard and there is no point pretending otherwise — start it here because this repo is about to publish.
userStories.notes: README's `Stubbed:` list was the one live contradiction left and is gone: verified in the tree before rewriting, not assumed — ios/Sources/Amphora/Store/SQLiteUploadStore.swift is a real SQLite actor (CREATE TABLE upload_jobs/resume_data, prepared statements), StorageGovernor.swift:64 writeRemainder and :122 exportPhotosAsset exist, Core/SourceResolver.swift handles ph:// via PHAsset, and android core/SourceResolver.kt:66 openFileDescriptor + Os.lseek streams seekable content:// with stageIfRequired:84 behind the StorageManager reservation. Replaced with what is genuinely missing (the RN spec AmphoraSpec has no native implementation) rather than deleting the line. 'Nothing moves bytes yet' needed no change in either direction: 120 already rewrote the Status section and grep across all *.md for 'Nothing moves'/'nothing has moved'/'No conformance vectors yet' returns 0 hits; the section states bytes moved 2026-08-27 with the Swift SIGKILL resume from offset 5505024 and the Kotlin CI run 33044191974 from offset 6553600. CLAUDE.md (181 lines) covers all four named points: no-chunk-temp-files as a commitment with its I6 enforcement, the local-SKIP vs CI-FAIL policy including the fact that Gradle always SKIPS on this machine so '3 passed, 1 skipped' is not green, the .executableTarget gotcha OBSERVED not quoted (swift test --package-path ios prints "error: no tests found; create a target in the 'Tests' directory" and exits 1, while swift run --package-path ios AmphoraPathTests reports 46 passed), and the adopt-the-protocol/build-the-clients boundary with the three things that fall on the wrong side of it. Added a fifth point not in the criterion but load-bearing: CI's Swift builds -warnings-as-errors and is stricter than the local toolchain, so verify.sh can be green while the ios job is red on the same commit. CHANGELOG.md (171 lines) started, Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 + SemVer, everything under [Unreleased] because git tag is empty and nothing is published; dated 2026-08-27 / 08-26 / 08-20 from the merge commits, with pre-08-27 entries explicitly marked as reconstructed from git history and tasks/chief/completed/, a 'Corrected' subsection for tasklist 80's false record, and a closing 'Known-red at the time of writing' section so a reader meets run 33044503283's ios+android FAILURE in the changelog rather than discovering it. Both indexed in docs/README.md ('unlinked is unreachable') and linked from README.md; ROADMAP phase 7's 'a CHANGELOG.md with a real first entry' precondition updated now that the file exists. Verify: .chief/verify.sh 3 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed - PASS Swift build, PASS Swift tests (46 passed), PASS TypeScript typecheck, SKIPPED Gradle (no JDK on PATH). Also ran the three cheap CI gates directly: check-single-fixture.sh PASS, verify-skip-policy.sh 'all assertions passed', check:control-surface 'spec remains control-surface only'. Link check across README/CLAUDE/CHANGELOG/ROADMAP/docs README/licensing: 64 links and anchors checked, 0 broken. Docs-only change touching nothing Android-shaped, so the Gradle skip leaves nothing in this story unverified.
